cards.text: Isaiah the prophet has another burden from the LORD, and this one is against Tyre, a famous city on the sea. He calls out first to the ships of Tarshish. Friend, when a prophet's message has your city's name in the very first line, you put the cookie DOWN.

cards.question: Isaiah's message against Tyre opens with the ships of Tarshish. He tells them to ___.
Why should the ships of Tarshish wail?

answers.text: Tyre is laid waste with no house or harbor
Tyre has closed its harbor to their ships
Tyre has gone to war against Tarshish

cards.text: No house. No harbor. And somebody out there has to break the news to those ships.

cards.question: Word about Tyre reaches the ships of Tarshish from the land of Cyprus.

cards.text: Then Isaiah calls out, 'O dwellers of the coastland, you merchants of Sidon,' whose traders crossed the sea. And his instructions are not what you'd expect in a crisis.

cards.question: Isaiah tells the dwellers of the coastland, the merchants of Sidon, to be silent.

cards.text: Isaiah remembers Tyre's glory days, when ships brought grain from Shihor over the great waters and the harvest of the Nile was Tyre's revenue. That's a paycheck that pulls up by BOAT, friend, and the only thing that ever pulled up to my drawer was a takeout menu.

cards.question: With ships bringing the Nile's harvest to her, Isaiah says Tyre was the ___ of the nations.

cards.text: Now Isaiah turns back to Sidon, the stronghold of the sea. And he did NOT bring a sympathy card.

cards.question: With Tyre laid waste, Isaiah tells Sidon, the stronghold of the sea, to be ___.

cards.text: Why? Because the sea has spoken: 'I have not been in labor or given birth. I have not raised young men or brought up young women.'

cards.question: The report about Tyre reaches Egypt, the land whose Nile harvest flowed to Tyre. How will Egypt take the news?

answers.text: They will cheer in the streets
They will send ships to help

cards.text: Isaiah tells the people of the coastland to cross over to Tarshish and wail. Then he looks at what's left and asks, is this your jubilant city?

cards.question: Isaiah says Tyre is a young city that was only recently built.

cards.text: Tyre's feet took her far away to settle, and now Isaiah asks who planned this against Tyre, the bestower of crowns, whose traders are princes and whose merchants are famous all over the earth. Her traders were PRINCES, friend, and the best deal I ever made was getting the spot in the drawer that wasn't under the dead batteries I shared it with.

cards.question: Isaiah asks who planned this against Tyre. Who does he say planned it?
Why did the LORD of Hosts plan this against Tyre?

answers.text: To disgrace all the renowned of the earth
To hand its harbor over to Sidon
To repay it for a broken treaty

cards.text: Isaiah turns to the Daughter of Tarshish and tells her to cultivate her land like the Nile. That's a BIG career change, and I say that as a cookie stamper whose last career change was going from stamping cookies to lying in a junk drawer.

cards.question: Why does Isaiah tell the Daughter of Tarshish to cultivate her land like the Nile?

answers.text: There is no longer a harbor
Egypt wants to buy her crops

cards.text: The LORD has stretched out His hand over the sea and made kingdoms tremble. KINGDOMS, friend, and I get the shakes when the oven timer goes off early.

cards.question: With His hand stretched out over the sea, the LORD has given a command that the strongholds of Canaan be ___.

cards.text: The LORD says, 'You shall rejoice no more, O oppressed Virgin Daughter of Sidon.' Then He tells her to get up and cross over to Cyprus.

cards.question: The LORD tells the Virgin Daughter of Sidon to cross over to Cyprus. What does He say she will find there?

cards.text: Then Isaiah points to the land of the Chaldeans, a people now of no account. Siege towers went up, its palaces were stripped, and it was destined for the desert creatures.

cards.question: Isaiah says it was the Assyrians who brought the land of the Chaldeans to ruin.

cards.text: And then that cry again: 'Wail, O ships of Tarshish, for your harbor has been destroyed!' Same ships, same wailing, and I bet those ships were hoping round two had better news.
Then Isaiah looks ahead and says Tyre will be forgotten. Friend, nobody does forgotten like a stamper who lived in the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: Isaiah says Tyre will be forgotten for ___ years, the span of a king's life.

cards.text: At the end of those years, it will happen to Tyre as in the song of the harlot. The song goes, 'Take up your harp, stroll through the city, O forgotten harlot. Make sweet melody, sing many a song…'

cards.question: In the song, why does the forgotten harlot take up her harp and sing many a song?

answers.text: So she can leave the city
So the king will pardon her

cards.text: At the end of seventy years, the LORD will restore Tyre. Forgotten, then restored? Friend, I know that story, and I STILL can't believe it happened to ME.

cards.question: Once the LORD restores her, Tyre goes back to selling herself to all the kingdoms on the face of the earth.

cards.text: But hold on, because the last verse has a turn I did NOT see coming. Watch where Tyre's money ends up.

cards.question: Tyre is back in business, but her profits and wages will be set apart to the ___.
Tyre's profit goes to those who live before the LORD. What will it give them?

answers.text: New ships and a safe harbor

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: “No house.”, “No harbor.”, and “And somebody out there has to break the news to those ships.” Non-opening story cards are limited to one or two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
